Subject: Request: Demo across US/EU/APAC execs — windows & DST concerns

Hi Dylan + team,

Thanks for taking this on. We're trying to lock a single 60-minute demo with our execs between Oct 25 and Nov 5. Important constraints: our CEO (Berlin local morning) wants a European-friendly time, but our CFO (Tokyo) can only do late-afternoon JST. SF execs prefer morning PDT.

Two things I'm worried about:
- EU daylight saving time ends on Oct 31 this year — that shift will move Berlin an hour relative to both SF and Tokyo on Nov 1.
- We have limited EA coordination windows and would prefer a date that won't require re-invites or awkward follow-ups during the cutover.

Can you share 3 candidate slots that:
1) fall within Oct 25–Nov 5,
2) avoid the Oct 31 DST cross-over if possible, and
3) include conversions for PDT / CEST / JST so our EAs can make a quick decision?

I've attached a quick stakeholder CSV with EAs and preferred times. Our EA (calendars@orbital-tech.com) is copied.

Cheers,
Anna Lin
Head of Platform — Orbital Tech

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear brief and the stakeholder list.

High level: we agree it's best to avoid any date that straddles the EU DST change (Oct 31). Below are three candidate windows that keep consistent local expectations across zones (I include local conversions). All times are 60-min slots and assume a 15-minute handoff/buffer at start for exec-runthroughs.

Option A — Tue Oct 26 (preferred)
- UTC: 15:00–16:00
- PDT (SF): 08:00–09:00
- CEST (Berlin): 17:00–18:00
- JST (Tokyo): 00:00–01:00 (next day) — late for Tokyo exec, so probably not ideal

Option B — Thu Oct 28 (balanced)
- UTC: 14:00–15:00
- PDT (SF): 07:00–08:00
- CEST (Berlin): 16:00–17:00
- JST (Tokyo): 23:00–00:00 (next day) — still late but within exec availability you mentioned

Option C — Mon Nov 1 (post-cutover, riskier)
- UTC: 15:00–16:00
- PDT (SF): 08:00–09:00
- CET (Berlin, after DST ends): 16:00–17:00
- JST (Tokyo): 00:00–01:00 (next day)

Notes:
- Option C would require re-invites on Nov 1 because Europe will have switched to CET on Oct 31; times are functionally the same wall-clock but calendar representations change and EAs sometimes get confused.
- Given your ask to avoid DST friction, we recommend Option B (Thu Oct 28) as a safe, pre-cutover choice.

I've attached a brief demo agenda (redwood-demo-agenda.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan (will attach the XLSX once we have stakeholder sign-off). If you confirm Option B, we'll send a calendar invite with a 10-minute buffer at the top for exec intros + a 15-minute post-demo debrief for internal follow-ups.

Proposed immediate next step: please let us know which option your EAs prefer; if you need earlier/later variants we can shift by an hour or add a second short session to accommodate Tokyo.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks

Quick note on the DST mechanics so the scheduling rationale is crystal clear for everyone and the EAs:
- EU switches from CEST to CET at 02:00 on Sun, Oct 31. That means any calendar invites spanning Oct 31 -> Nov 1 can show different local times depending on how the invite is stored/edited and which client interprets it.
- Best practice: avoid creating invites on Oct 31 that reference times after 02:00 local; and avoid selecting Nov 1 as the date if you want to preserve the same wall-clock times across regions.

So: endorsing Dylan and Monica's call to prefer Oct 26–Oct 29 window. Oct 28 works well for our product VP and is the least risky for cross-region confusion.

If we confirm Oct 28, I'll ask our scheduling ops to:
- Publish the event in UTC and include explicit local conversions in the invite body.
- Add the line: "Note: Europe DST ends on 2027-10-31; this event is scheduled before that cutover."

That should reduce the number of re-invite/resync requests from EAs.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Strategy — Redwood Inference
